## Background

This Class we will be running thru an entire DESeq2 analysis using the `DESeq2` package. These skills where developed in the previous class(13) and are exapanded down below.

## Data Import 
read counts & metadata CSV files 

```{r import}
metadata<- read.csv("GSE37704_metadata.csv", row.names=1)
counts<- read.csv("GSE37704_featurecounts.csv", row.names=1)
```

```{r}
metadata
# Need to remove the "length" column in `counts`
head(counts)
```

## Sannity Check 

> Q. Complete the code below to remove the troublesome first column from countData

```{r}
countData <- as.matrix(counts[,-1])
head(countData)
```

```{r}
all(colnames(countData)== metadata$id)
```

> Q. Complete the code below to filter countData to exclude genes (i.e. rows) where we have 0 read count across all samples (i.e. columns).

When we sum across the rows using `rowSums()` function and the answer is 0 this means w have 0 counts for that gene in all experiments.

```{r}
to.keep<- rowSums(countData)!=0
countData = countData[to.keep, ]
head(countData)
```

```{r}
dim(countData)
```

## Set up DESeq object 

```{r, warning=FALSE}
library(DESeq2)

dds=DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = countData,
                           colData = metadata ,
                           design = ~condition)
```

## Run DESeq analysis pipeline 
```{r}
dds<-DESeq(dds)
res<- results(dds)
```

## Extract Results 
big table with log2fold changes and p-value 

```{r}
dds<-DESeq(dds)
res<- results(dds)
head(res)
```
## Data visulization 
Volcano plot 

```{r}
my_cols<-rep("gray",nrow(res))
my_cols[abs(res$log2FoldChange)> 2]<- "red"
my_cols[res$padj>0.05]<- "grey"
```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(res)+
  aes(log2FoldChange,-log(padj))+
  geom_point(alpha=0.3, color=my_cols)+
  geom_vline(xintercept= c(-2,+2), col="blue")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log(0.05), col="blue")
```

## Add annotation data 
add gene symbols and entrez ids 

```{r}
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
```

```{r}
columns(org.Hs.eg.db)
res$symbol<-mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
      keys=row.names(res),
       keytype="ENSEMBL", 
      column="SYMBOL",
      multiVals = "first")
res$name<-mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
      keys=row.names(res),
       keytype="ENSEMBL", 
      column="GENENAME",
      multiVals = "first")
res$entrez<-mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
      keys=row.names(res),
       keytype="ENSEMBL", 
      column="ENTREZID",
      multiVals = "first")
head(res,10)
```

> Q. Finally for this section let's reorder these results by adjusted p-value and save them to a CSV file in your current project directory.

```{r}
res = res[order(res$pvalue),]
write.csv(res, file ="deseq_results.csv")
```

## Pathway analysis 
KEGG, GO and REACTOME

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(pathview)
library(gage)
library(gageData)
```

```{r}
data(kegg.sets.hs)
data(sigmet.idx.hs)
```

```{r}
foldchanges = res$log2FoldChange
names(foldchanges) = res$entrez
head(foldchanges)
```

```{r}
keggres=gage(foldchanges, gsets=kegg.sets.hs)
```

```{r}
pathview(gene.data=foldchanges, pathway.id="hsa04110")
```
![](hsa04110.pathview.png)
## Gene Ontology (GO)

```{r}
data(go.sets.hs)
data(go.subs.hs)

gobpsets = go.sets.hs[go.subs.hs$BP]

gobpres = gage(foldchanges, gsets=gobpsets)

lapply(gobpres, head)
```

## REACTOME 

There is an R package for this type of analysis 

to use the website you either paste or upload a list of differential expressed genes (DEGS):

```{r}
sig_genes <- res[res$padj <= 0.05 & !is.na(res$padj), "symbol"]
print(paste("Total number of significant genes:", length(sig_genes)))
write.table(sig_genes, file="significant_genes.txt", row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
```
> Q: What pathway has the most significant “Entities p-value”? Do the most significant pathways listed match your previous KEGG results? What factors could cause differences between the two methods?

The most significant `entities p-val` (lowest p-val) is the SMAC(DIABLO)-mediated dissociation of IAP- caspase complexes. This can be seen in the KEGG png, as smc1/3 which are both highlighted as green. All these pathways found in the REACTOME are also highlighted as green in the KEGG pathway illustration. The frequency that a database is updated could cause differences between the two methods, if one is relying on old outdated information it could lead to discrepancies. 

## Save .csv results 

```{r}
write.csv(res, file="myresults_annotated.csv")
```
